{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that face emotional valence perception would decrease with increasing eccentricity, and that eccentricity might have different effects on different valences due to potentially dissociated underlying mechanisms.",
  "design": "within",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Eccentricity (0°, 2°, 4°) and emotional valence (positive, neutral, negative) of facial stimuli.",
  "outcome_measure": "Categorization accuracy and response time (RT) for emotional valence.",
  "population_and_setting": "Adults with normal or corrected-to-normal vision, tested in a laboratory setting using a chin rest at a 60 cm viewing distance.",
  "sample_size_total": 51,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Participants were recruited and reimbursed for their efforts; the study was approved by the Bar Ilan University ethics committee.",
  "analysis_plan": "Two-way repeated-measures ANOVA with eccentricity and emotional valence as factors, followed by post-hoc analyses with Bonferroni adjustment.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "The block-design experiment presented sequences of 8 emotional images per block. Stimuli were 2° x 2.71° grayscale portraits from the Karolinska Directed Emotional Faces database. Eye movements were monitored to ensure fixation. Participants were instructed to report the dominant valence of the block."
